stumbles.quote: The retry count had been 0 since the refactor on 2026-09-14, so `execute()` never tried the request a second time.
stumbles.why: "The refactor" is never explained, so a first-time reader doesn't know which refactor this was or why it set the retry count to 0. "Retry count" is also ambiguous: it could mean a config value or a default.

stumbles.quote: Boot treated that 503 as a credential failure and printed "auth failed".
stumbles.why: "Boot" is not defined. It could be application startup or a boot script. The text also never says why a 503 was read as an auth error, and the fix doesn't mention changing that.

stumbles.quote: Any other status fails at once, as it did before.
stumbles.why: This conflicts with the Problem section, which says the retry count was 0 and so even 503 was not retried. The text doesn't say whether "before" means before the refactor or just before this change.

stumbles.quote: the error message names the status code
stumbles.why: The Change section never says error messages were changed. A reader can't tell whether this is new behavior or existing behavior. It also doesn't say whether the "auth failed" message is still printed on a 503.

stumbles.quote: up to 4 times, with jittered exponential backoff that starts at 0.5 s
stumbles.why: This is ambiguous. It could mean 4 retries (5 attempts in total) or 4 attempts. The test "four 503s, then failure" doesn't settle it, because it would fail after 4 attempts or after 5. The backoff multiplier and cap are also missing, and the "bounds" the timing test checks are never stated.

point: The PR adds retry with jittered exponential backoff on 503 and 429 to the Turso client's `execute()`, so cold-start 503s no longer fail boot, and it backs this with a 40-boot measurement and 6 tests.
